title: A piece's brief — visual-communication capability
description: Formal shape of a piece's `brief.yaml` (DEC-029 points 2 and 3): what the piece must show and why it is designed so, for whoever makes or reviews it. A part for the whole piece, and a part for each page it speaks of, keyed by the page's id. Each part holds relations, goals, a takeaway and reasons, and names the content by key paths. It holds no content, no value and no layout, and has no language. A person writes it; no command changes what it says, and no renderer reads it. The check reads what it names (DEC-029 point 5). Its top and each mapping in it keep the methodology's container `pkit` free. Document-shaped schema. Companion per COR-018.

pkit_schema.description: The schema that binds this file (COR-023; DEC-002 point 3): `visual-communication:brief`.

schema_version.description: The format number, shared by every schema of the capability (DEC-003 point 1).

piece.description: The part for the whole piece: what concerns the piece, or more than one of its pages, and the intent of a page not yet in the content. A piece of one page keeps all of it here, its takeaway included. Its key paths start at the content's top.

pages.description: A part for each page the brief speaks of, keyed by the id the page carries in the content. Its key paths start at the page.

container.description: The methodology's container (COR-053 point 10), which the capability never reads.

part.description: A part of the brief, for the whole piece or for one page (DEC-029 points 2 and 3).

relations.description: What a picture must make visible between the parts it shows, such as levels that each rest on the one below.

goals.description: What the piece, or the page, must achieve with its audience, such as what the audience can do after it.

takeaway.description: The one point a reader should leave the page with, written only where the page's content has no lead that states it.

reasons.description: Why each choice of the design was made, in the order of the aspects: structure, form, hierarchy, type, colour, space.

relation.description: A relation, in words, and the parts of the content it relates, by their key paths. A part a key path cannot reach, inside a local component or in shared content, is named in the words alone.

relates.description: The parts of the content the relation is between, each by its key path.

reason.description: Why one choice of the design was made, and the principle it rests on (DEC-029 point 2).

aspect.description: What the choice is about: `structure`, what the content's structure is; `form`, the form chosen for it and the visual variables that carry the structure; `hierarchy`, what is seen first and what is ranked below it; `type`, `colour` and `space`, the brand's roles of each that the page takes, and what each colour marks.

about.description: The part of the page, or of the piece, the reason is about, by its key path. Without it, the reason is about the whole page, or the whole piece.

text.description: Why the choice was made, in words.

principle.description: The principle the choice rests on, by its name and its source.

source.description: Where the principle is set out, such as an author and a work.

key-path.description: A part of the content by the keys and ids that lead to it, never its place in a list (DEC-011 point 3): each key joined by `.`, and in each list the item by its id, as `[<id>]`.
